This page is a plain-language summary, not the licence itself. The [LICENSE](../LICENSE) file is the only binding document — if this page and the LICENSE ever disagree, the LICENSE governs.

## ✅ What the MIT License lets you do

MIT is permissive. It grants anyone the right to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and sell Notploy, for free or for money. In practice that means:

- Run Notploy yourself for personal, internal, or commercial purposes.
- Modify it and keep your modifications private. MIT does not require you to publish your changes.
- Offer a modified Notploy as a paid or free hosted service. MIT has no network-use clause, so running it as a service does not oblige you to release your source.
- Redistribute it, on its own or bundled into a larger product, and charge for that.
- Use it in a commercial setting with no purchase, no license key, and no obligation to open-source anything.

The only obligation MIT imposes is to keep the copyright and permission notice intact in copies or substantial portions of the software.

To be explicit about a common misconception: **MIT has no copyleft obligations.** Source-disclosure duties, including for network use, belong to the GPL, AGPL, and SSPL — not to this project.

## 🚫 What the MIT License does not cover

The MIT License covers the source code in this repository. It does not cover three other things:

- **Trademarks.** "Notploy" and "Sky Genesis Enterprise" are marks of Sky Genesis Enterprise. The license lets you redistribute and modify the code; it does not let you ship it under those names. If you rebrand, use your own product name and domain.
- **Paid plans, license keys, and support.** Not everything Sky Genesis Enterprise offers is free. These are commercial products described below, and obtaining one requires a subscription, a license key, or a signed agreement — not a source license.
- **Warranty and liability.** The software is provided "AS IS", without warranty of any kind, as stated in the LICENSE text.

## 💼 What is actually a paid product

Notploy ships in four editions. They share the same deployment engine and the same MIT-licensed source code. What differs is who operates the Notploy control plane and which team and compliance features are enabled. See [Cloud vs Self-Hosted](https://docs.notploy.com/docs/core/differences) for the full comparison.

| Edition | Control plane | Enterprise features | How you get it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Self-Hosted (OSS) | You operate it | — | Free, no license key |
| Cloud | Notploy operates it | Plan-dependent | Subscription, from $4.50/mo |
| Enterprise Self-Hosted | You operate it | SSO, SCIM, custom roles, audit logs, Application Authentication, whitelabeling | License key issued by the Notploy team |
| Enterprise Cloud | Notploy operates it | SSO, SCIM, custom roles, audit logs, Application Authentication | Custom plan |

The Enterprise feature code is part of this MIT-licensed repository and is gated at runtime by a license key. A license key is a paid key, not a restriction on your rights under the MIT License.

If you want the enterprise capabilities but would rather not operate a Notploy instance yourself, the route is a Cloud plan or an Enterprise license — not a commercial source license.

## 🧾 When you would contact us for an agreement

You do not need one to use, modify, host, or sell Notploy. You would contact us to:

- Get an Enterprise license key, or an Enterprise Cloud plan.
- Buy a paid Cloud plan — see [pricing](https://notploy.com/pricing).
- Get support with an SLA, priority bug fixes, custom integrations, or feature development — see [SUPPORT.md](./SUPPORT.md).
- Ship Notploy under your own brand and domain. The whitelabeling capability rebrands the interface; using the Notploy name itself requires written permission.
- Request a trademark permission, or a license on different terms for a specific scenario.
